title: Azure Virtual Desktop Session Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `azure:diagnostics` events with `Category="WVDConnections"` into `index=cloud`. Confirm UC-4.2.52 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `azure:diagnostics` traffic without `Category="WVDConnections"`. Confirm UC-4.2.52 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.2.52 — Azure Virtual Desktop Session Health: queries Microsoft Azure `azure:diagnostics` for search criteria `Category="WVDConnections"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Virtual Desktop Session Health' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.52 drives high-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable diagnostics on AVD host pools to route `WVDConnections`, `WVDErrors`, and `WVDCheckpoints` to Splunk. Monitor connection success rate, average session duration, and round-trip time. Alert on connection failure spikes, session host unavailability, and high input delay (>200ms). knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) with the modular input for `azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable diagnostics on AVD host pools to route `WVDConnections`, `WVDErrors`, and `WVDCheckpoints` to Splunk. Monitor connection success rate, average session duration, and round-trip time. Alert on connection failure spikes, session host unavailability, and high input delay (>200ms). Track session host resource utilization (CPU, memory, disk) from Azure Monitor metrics.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="WVDConnections"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.52_azure_virtual_desktop_se_52"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:diagnostics` in `index=cloud` to detect azure virtual desktop session health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_52_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (session hosts with errors), Line chart (connections and failures over time), Single value (active sessions)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure virtual desktop session health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
